items.name: text!
items.docs: The body as UTF-8 text, to `default_max` bytes.

items.name: json!
items.docs: The body as JSON, to `default_max` bytes. A parse error is `BadData` (MODULES.md 15).

items.name: bytes!
items.docs: The bytes of the body, to `default_max` bytes.

items.name: bytes_with!
items.docs:
The bytes of the body, to `max_bytes`. More is `TooLarge`. A stream: one wait, and JS checks the size
before the copy into wasm (`pf.readUpTo`), so a body over the limit takes no wasm memory.

items.name: chunk!
items.docs:
The next chunk of a stream, as JS gives it, cut to `default_max` (MC11). One wait.
`Empty`, `Text` and `Bytes` are one chunk (none for `Empty`), with no crossing: a value is not a stream, so
each call on the same value gives the same chunk.

items.name: tee!
items.docs: Two bodies with the same bytes. A stream: `ReadableStream.tee()`, no wait. A stream that was read is `BodyErr`.

items.name: sha256!
items.docs:
The SHA-256 of the body (32 bytes). A stream: `crypto.DigestStream` in JS, one wait, no copy into wasm.
`Text` and `Bytes`: the builtin `Crypto.SHA256` in wasm, no crossing.

items.name: writer!
items.docs:
A stream that the task writes, for example in the work of `Response.after` (API.md 10.2): `pf.writer`, a
`TransformStream`, no wait. The 30 s limit after the response starts at `close!`.

items.name: compress!
items.docs:
`pipeThrough(new CompressionStream(format))`, no wait. A `Text` or `Bytes` body becomes a stream first.
The result is a `Stream`: the bytes stay in JS.

items.name: decompress!
items.docs: `pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream(format))`, no wait. As `compress!`.

items.name: Writer
items.docs: The writable side of a `writer!` stream. It holds a ref, so it is good for one task (MC13).
items.head: Writer

items.name: write
items.docs:
One wait: until the stream takes the chunk (the reader asked for it, MC3). After `close!`: `BodyErr`.
The twin gives an `Io`, so a write can run next to the read of the stream (`Io.race!`, `Io.start!`).

items.name: write_text
items.docs: The text as UTF-8 (a stream of a response takes bytes only).

items.name: close!
items.docs: No wait. The body is complete now (API.md 10.2): the 30 s limit after `respond!` starts.

items.name: default
items.docs: `caches.default`.

items.name: named
items.docs: `caches.open(name)`, in the program of each call: it gives data (MC1), not a promise.

items.name: get
items.docs:
`cache.match(url)`. The body is a stream (`Http.open!`): `res.text!()` is one more wait. A key that is not
cached: `NotFound` (OP7: `Fields` of the `undefined` result).

items.name: put
items.docs:
`cache.put(url, response)`, then the response to send. A `Stream` body is read by the put, so the program tees it
first (`ReadableStream.tee()`): one branch goes to the cache, and the response that `put` gives has the other.
Send that response, not the one given. The put reads its branch to the end, so the branch of the response holds the
whole body in JS until it is sent: for a large stream use `put_after!`. Other bodies: the same response.
A 206 response or a response with `Vary: *` is `CacheErr` (a throw). A response that is not cached
(`Set-Cookie`, `no-store`, too large) is `Ok`: `put` does not say it (Cloudflare docs).

items.name: put_after!
items.docs:
Put after the response (API.md 10.2): tee a `Stream` body now (one `call!`, no wait), and give the response to
send, with `Response.after` work that puts the other branch. The client and the cache read at the same time, so
the tee holds only the bytes that one reads before the other. An `Err` of the put is the log line
`fetch: after respond: failed: ...`. Only for the response of a `fetch!` handler: elsewhere the work does not run.

items.name: delete
items.docs: `cache.delete(url)`: `false` is `NotFound`.

items.name: Bytes
items.docs:
Bytes that cross as a CBOR byte string (major type 2). A `List(U8)` writes as an array of numbers.
It reads a byte string or an array of integers 0 to 255: a D1 BLOB, which JS gives as an array, reads into it.
`Cbor.bytes(list)` makes one (an alias has no constructor: `Cbor.Bytes.(list)` gives "expected nominal type"), and `bytes.to_list()` gives the list back.
The same type as `Bytes` of the package.
items.head: Bytes

items.name: Options
items.docs:
The options of `parse_with`: `{ fields ?: [Snake, Camel], int_from_text ?: Bool }`. Each field is optional: `{}` is the same as `parse`.
The same type as `Options` of the package.
items.head: Options

items.name: Step
items.docs:

The same type as `Step` of the package.
items.head: Step

items.name: Format
items.docs:
The encoding value. A custom `parser_for` or `encoder_for` in an app takes it as its argument:
`parser_for : Cbor.Format -> (Cbor.State -> Try({ value : T, rest : Cbor.State }, [InvalidCbor(U64)]))`.
The methods of the codec protocol (`enc.parse_str(state)`) are found by static dispatch on it.
The same type as `Cbor` of the package.
items.head: Format

items.name: State
items.docs:
The read position of a parse. A custom `parser_for` passes it from step to step. Its fields are hidden.
The same type as `State` of the package.
items.head: State

items.name: bytes
items.docs: Makes `Bytes` from a list: the same as `CborPkg.Bytes.(list)` of the package.

items.name: parse
items.docs:
Reads one CBOR item of the type `a` from all of `raw`. The type comes from the annotation.
The error is `InvalidCbor(pos)`, with the byte position of the problem, or `MissingRequiredField(name)` from the
derived parser of a record. Bytes after the item are an error at the position of the first extra byte.

items.name: parse_camel
items.docs: Like `parse`, with record fields in camelCase: `user_id` is read from `userId`.

items.name: parse_with
items.docs:
Like `parse`, with options: `{ fields: Snake, int_from_text: Bool.False }`. Each field is optional, `{}` is the same as `parse`.
`int_from_text: Bool.True` reads an integer type also from text that is a canonical decimal integer in its range.

items.name: path_at
items.docs:
The path from the root to the item that starts at byte `pos`: the array indexes and the map keys.
Use it with the position of `InvalidCbor(pos)` to find the field of the error.
The path of the root is `[]`. `Err(NotFound)` when no item starts at `pos`.

items.name: encode
items.docs: Writes `value` as one CBOR item. It cannot fail. A `Secret` in `value` does not compile.

items.name: wait_until!
items.docs:
Start the operation now (`Io.start!`) and give its promise to `ctx.waitUntil`, in one `call!`. The reader of
the `Io` does not run, so its result is dropped: only an `Io({}, e)` fits, and an operation with a result (for
example `cache.put`, which gives the response to send) is a type error. A Roc-level `Err` is not seen. A JS throw
goes to the log. The context of the task stays until the operation settles, or until the 30 s limit of
`waitUntil` (API.md 6.5, RS1).

items.name: pass_through!
items.docs:
`ctx.passThroughOnException()`: after it, an `Err` of the `fetch` handler makes the shim throw, so Workers
sends the request to the origin. Only in the `Fetch` of a Worker. Elsewhere `InvalidState`.

runtime answers through a stub, so the call waits (`await!`). A throw is dropped: there is no `Try`.

items.docs: A shape that is not in the table is a platform bug: a crash, with the text in the log.

items.name: finish!
items.docs:
The outcome for JS (`main.roc`). A `Respond` with `after_work!` (`Response.after`, API.md 10.2): the response goes
to the `respond` hook of the entry now (`pf.respond`), then the work runs in the same task, and its result is the
outcome (`Done`, or `Failed` with the text of the error).

items.name: var!
items.docs: A text var. A name that is not set, or a var that is not text (a JSON var), is `MissingEnv`.

items.name: json!
items.docs:
A JSON var: an object of the Wrangler config (`JSON.stringify` in JS, then `Json.parse`), or a text var with
JSON text. A value that does not fit the type is `BadData`.

items.name: secret!
items.docs: A secret (a text var of `wrangler secret put`) as a `Secret`, so it does not show in a log line.

items.name: native!
items.signature: U32, List(U8) => { status : U8, bytes : List(U8) }
items.docs: A native op of the host (API.md 8, PLAN.md 8e). Apps use `Native`.

items.name: send
items.docs: `fetch(request)`, and the body to `Body.default_max` bytes: one wait.

items.name: send_with
items.signature: Request, { max_bytes ?: U64, timeout_ms ?: U64, cf ?: Js } -> Io(Response, [Infra([Network(Io.Thrown), HttpErr(Io.Thrown), TooLarge])])
items.docs:
`max_bytes`: the limit of the body (default `Body.default_max`). `timeout_ms`: `AbortSignal.timeout`, a timeout
is `Network`. `cf`: the `cf` options of `fetch` (`cacheTtl`, `cacheEverything`), a `Js` object of the app.

items.name: send_with!
items.signature: Request, { max_bytes ?: U64, timeout_ms ?: U64, cf ?: Js } => Try(Response, [Infra([Network(Io.Thrown), HttpErr(Io.Thrown), TooLarge])])

items.name: open
items.docs: `fetch(request)`: the body stays a stream in JS (a `Stream` body, MC13), for a large body or a pass-through.

items.name: get
items.docs: `send` of a `GET` of the URL.

items.name: CfError
items.docs:
What Cloudflare answers for a request that it cannot pass on (MODULES.md 4): the `status` and the `code` of the
text `error code: <code>`.
items.head: CfError

items.name: cloudflare_error
items.docs:
Is this answer an error page of Cloudflare, not of the origin? `Http.send!` gives `Ok` for a DNS failure
(530, `error code: 1016`) and a blocked address (403, `error code: 1003`). Pure: the status is 400 or more, and the
body is a text or bytes of 64 bytes or less that reads `error code: ` and digits (the body of `send!` is always
bytes). A `Stream` body (`open!`) is not read: `NotCloudflareError`.

items.name: error
items.docs:
MC9, table "Named error tags": a `TypeError` is a bad request (URL, scheme, header), each other throw of
`fetch` is no response. The limit of `pf.readUpTo` is `TooLarge`.

items.name: declare
items.signature: Hyperdrive -> { name : Str, kind : Str, props : List((Str, Str)) }
items.docs: The binding for the manifest (`Worker.new({ bindings: [...] })`, MODULES.md 3): the kind `hyperdrive`.

items.name: Config
items.signature: { connection_string : Secret, host : Str, port : U16, user : Str, password : Secret, database : Str }
items.docs: What Workers gives for a database: the connection string and its parts. The two secrets do not show in a log line.
items.head: Config

items.name: config!
items.docs: A binding that is not in the config gives `undefined` fields (OP7): a crash with the name of the binding.

items.name: connect
items.docs:
`env[name].connect()`, then a wait for `opened` (`pf.tcpOpen`): one wait. The socket goes to the database of the
binding through Hyperdrive. A throw (no binding, the origin does not answer) is `SocketErr`.

items.name: from_u64
items.docs: The same bits as the U64. No loss, no error: the whole U64 range maps to the whole I64 range.

items.name: from_bytes
items.docs: 8 bytes, big-endian (the prefix of a SHA-256). Another length is `Err(BadLength)`.

items.name: from_str
items.docs:
Decimal text, canonical (`0`, or `-?[1-9][0-9]*`), as the I64 (-2^63 to 2^63-1) or as the U64 (2^63 to 2^64-1).
The two ranges share no text except 0 to 2^63-1, where both mean the same value: there is no ambiguity.

items.name: to_bytes
items.docs: 8 bytes, big-endian.

items.name: to_str
items.docs: The decimal text of the I64. It is the text that SQL and CBOR use.

items.name: to_u64_str
items.docs: The decimal text of the U64. It is the text that a browser sees (JSON).

items.name: to_web
items.docs: The same id for an API payload: any format writes the U64 text. A field `id : Id64.Web` in a response record.

items.name: from_web
items.docs: Reads the id of an API payload.

items.name: parser_for
items.signature:
encoding -> (state -> Try({ value : Id64, rest : state }, err))
		where [
			encoding.parse_str : encoding, state -> Try({ value : Str, rest : state }, err),
			encoding.parse_i64 : encoding, state -> Try({ value : I64, rest : state }, err),
			# Marker, never called: only a binary format has it. `Encoding.Json` has no `parse_bytes`.
			encoding.parse_bytes : encoding, state -> Try({ value : List(U8), rest : state }, err),
		]
items.docs:
Reads decimal text, or else a CBOR integer (`parse_i64`). The state is a value, so the second try starts at the same item.
CBOR only (see the marker): JSON would also give a number, which a browser has already rounded above 2^53. Read `Id64.Web` there.

items.name: encoder_for
items.signature:
encoding -> (Id64, state -> Try(state, err))
		where [
			encoding.encode_str : Str, state -> Try(state, err),
			# Marker, never called: only a binary format has it. `Encoding.Json` has no `encode_bytes`, so an `Id64` in a JSON
			# value does not compile: it would show the I64 text (negative above 2^63) to a browser. Use `Id64.Web` there.
			encoding.encode_bytes : List(U8), state -> Try(state, err),
		]
items.docs: Writes the decimal text of the I64 (R-IK2). CBOR only (see the marker).

items.name: Web
items.docs: An id for a browser: it writes the U64 text in any format (JSON too), and reads text only.
items.head: Web

items.name: parser_for
items.signature:
encoding -> (state -> Try({ value : Id64.Web, rest : state }, err))
			where [
				encoding.parse_str : encoding, state -> Try({ value : Str, rest : state }, err),
				# Called only to get the error of the format for a bad text (an item of text is never an integer).
				encoding.parse_i64 : encoding, state -> Try({ value : I64, rest : state }, err),
			]
items.docs: Reads U64 or I64 text in any format. A number (a JSON number, a CBOR integer) is an error: an id in JSON must be text.

items.name: encoder_for
items.signature:
encoding -> (Id64.Web, state -> Try(state, err))
			where [
				encoding.encode_str : Str, state -> Try(state, err),
			]

items.name: Io
items.signature: { ops : List(Js.Op), waits : Bool, read : Try(Js, Io.Thrown) -> Try(a, e) }
items.head: Io(a, e)

items.name: Thrown
items.docs: What JS threw: the name and the message of the error (API.md 4, status 1).
items.head: Thrown

items.name: new
items.signature: List(Js.Op), (Try(Js, Io.Thrown) -> Try(a, e)) -> Io(a, e)
items.docs: Low level: an operation from `Js` ops, that runs with `Js.await!` (one JSPI wait).

items.name: sync
items.signature: List(Js.Op), (Try(Js, Io.Thrown) -> Try(a, e)) -> Io(a, e)
items.docs: Low level: an operation from `Js` ops, that runs with `Js.call!` (no wait). A promise in it is an error (status 2).

items.name: recover
items.signature: Io(a, e), (e -> Try(a, f)) -> Io(a, f)
items.docs: Handle an error: `Ok` gives a value in place of it, `Err` gives the error of the new type (`Try.on_err`).

items.name: run!
items.docs: The usual call: one crossing.

items.name: both!
items.signature: Io(a, e), Io(b, e) => Try((a, b), e)
items.docs: Two operations at the same time, in one crossing (`Par`, OP6).

items.name: all!
items.docs: Many operations at the same time, in one crossing (`Par`, OP6).

items.name: race!
items.signature: List(Io(a, e)) => { index : U64, result : Try(a, e) }
items.docs:
The first operation to settle wins (`Race`, OP8). `index` is its place in the list.
The others are aborted. A `Race` with no branch is a bad program (status 3).

items.name: timeout
items.docs:
The operation, or `Err(Infra(TimedOut))` when `ms` pass first: a race with a sleep (`Race`, OP8). The loser is aborted
as in `race!` (a receive that lost takes no message). The sleep is the one of `Time.sleep`.

items.name: timeout_at
items.docs:
The same as `timeout`, with a point in time: `deadline_ms` is on the clock of `Time.now_ms!` (`Date.now()`).
One deadline for many reads needs no sum of the time left. The wait is `max(0, deadline_ms - Date.now())` at
the time the program runs (`pf.waitUntil`), not when the `Io` is made. A deadline in the past waits 0 ms:
the operation wins only when it has a result already, else the answer is `Err(Infra(TimedOut))` at once.

items.name: start!
items.docs:
Start an operation, and give its promise as a ref (for `Ctx.wait_until!`). No wait.
The reader does not run: a Roc-level `Err` is not seen. A JS throw goes to the log (6.5).

items.name: Js
items.signature:
[
	Undefined,
	Null,
	Bool(Bool),
	Num(F64),
	Int(I64),
	Text(Str),
	Bytes(List(U8)),
	Arr(List(Js)),
	Obj(List((Str, Js))),
	Ref(Js.Ref),
	Error(Str, Str),
	## One value as CBOR, for typed data (API.md 5.2).
	Packed(List(U8)),
]
items.docs:
The escape hatch (API.md 5, 6): a JS value that crosses the bridge, the ops of a program that JS runs (API.md 6.2),
the raw runs of a program (`await!`, `call!`), and the pin table. An app uses it only for a Workers API that no
module has. To make an `Io` from ops, use `Io.new` and `Io.sync` (`Io` imports `Js`, so they cannot be here).
The Zig host encodes and decodes the CBOR form (API.md 5.1). Roc never sees the bytes.
items.head: Js

items.name: Ref
items.docs:
The id of a JS object in the ref table of the task (API.md 9). `==` compares ids (RS1).
A record backing, so a ref has no codec (MODULES.md MC13, 15).
items.head: Ref

items.name: Target
items.docs: Where an op finds its object: a root of the task (OP3), an earlier slot, or a ref.
items.head: Target

items.name: Arg
items.docs: An op argument: a value, or an earlier slot.
items.head: Arg

items.name: Op
items.signature:
[
		Get(Js.Target, Str),
		Set(Js.Target, Str, Js.Arg),
		Call(Js.Target, Str, List(Js.Arg)),
		Start(Js.Target, Str, List(Js.Arg)),
		New(Js.Target, Str, List(Js.Arg)),
		Fields(Js.Target, List(Str)),
		Keep(Js.Target),
		Array(List(Js.Arg)),
		Record(List((Str, Js.Arg))),
		Par(List(List(Js.Op))),
		Race(List(List(Js.Op))),
	]
items.docs: One op. Each op puts its result in the next slot (API.md 6.2).
items.head: Op

items.name: Thrown
items.docs: What JS threw: the name and the message of the error (API.md 4, status 1). `Io.Thrown` is this type.
items.head: Thrown

items.name: host_await!
items.docs:
The hosted functions (API.md 4): a program as one `Js` value in, the status 0 to 3 and the value out. Use
`await!` and `call!`.

items.name: host_call!
items.docs: A promise is status 2.

items.name: await!
items.docs: Run a program with one wait (API.md 6.4). The value of the last op, or what JS threw.

items.name: call!
items.docs: Run a program with no wait (API.md 6.4).

items.name: pin!
items.docs:
The pin table of the isolate (API.md RS2). `pin!` keeps the value for later tasks of this isolate by name: each
`Ref` in it keeps its object. A full table (shim option `pinLimit`) is `PinErr`. Each is one `call!`, no wait.

items.name: pinned!
items.docs:
The value that `pin!` kept (J1 to J7: each object gets a new ref of this task). `NotPinned`: no entry, or an
entry past its age.

items.name: unpin!
items.docs: Remove the entry. No entry: no change.

items.name: program
items.docs:
The ops as one `Js` array, the format that the JS interpreter reads (OP5):
`[["get", target, name], ["call", target, name, [args]], ...]`.

items.name: Kv
items.signature: { name : Str, write : a -> Try(Js, Str), read : List(U8) -> Try(a, Str) }
items.head: Kv(a)

items.name: json
items.docs: Values of the type `a`, as JSON text. A value that JSON cannot show (a `NaN` in an `F64`) is `BadData` of the put.

items.name: text
items.docs: Values that are text, as they are.

items.name: bytes
items.docs: Values that are bytes, as they are.

items.name: declare
items.signature: Kv(a) -> { name : Str, kind : Str, props : List((Str, Str)) }
items.docs: The binding for the manifest (`Worker.new({ bindings: [...] })`, MODULES.md 3): the kind `kv`.

items.name: get
items.signature: Kv(a), Str -> Io(a, [NotFound, Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str), TooLarge])])
items.docs: `get(key, { type: "stream" })` and the stream to `Body.default_max` bytes: one wait.

items.name: get!
items.signature: Kv(a), Str => Try(a, [NotFound, Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str), TooLarge])])

items.name: get_or
items.signature: Kv(a), Str, a -> Io(a, [Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str), TooLarge])])
items.docs: `get`, and `default` for a key that is not there. The other errors stay.

items.name: get_or!
items.signature: Kv(a), Str, a => Try(a, [Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str), TooLarge])])

items.name: find
items.docs: `get` that gives a missing key as `Ok(Err(NotFound))`, so the error type of the caller has no `NotFound`.

items.name: get_with
items.signature: Kv(a), Str, { cache_ttl_ms ?: U64, max_bytes ?: U64 } -> Io(a, [NotFound, Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str), TooLarge])])
items.docs: `cache_ttl_ms`: 30 s or more (KV throws for less: `KvErr`). `max_bytes`: the limit of the value.

items.name: get_with!
items.signature: Kv(a), Str, { cache_ttl_ms ?: U64, max_bytes ?: U64 } => Try(a, [NotFound, Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str), TooLarge])])

items.name: get_with_metadata
items.signature: Kv(a), Str -> Io({ value : a, metadata : Try(m, [Missing]) }, [NotFound, Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str), TooLarge])]) where [m.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs:
`getWithMetadata`. The type of the metadata comes from the annotation at the call (MC7). A key with no metadata
has `Err(Missing)` in `metadata`. KV stores the metadata as JSON.

items.name: get_with_metadata!
items.signature: Kv(a), Str => Try({ value : a, metadata : Try(m, [Missing]) }, [NotFound, Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str), TooLarge])]) where [m.Cbor.Readable(errs)]

items.name: get_with_metadata_with
items.signature: Kv(a), Str, { cache_ttl_ms ?: U64, max_bytes ?: U64 } -> Io({ value : a, metadata : Try(m, [Missing]) }, [NotFound, Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str), TooLarge])]) where [m.Cbor.Readable(errs)]

items.name: get_with_metadata_with!
items.signature: Kv(a), Str, { cache_ttl_ms ?: U64, max_bytes ?: U64 } => Try({ value : a, metadata : Try(m, [Missing]) }, [NotFound, Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str), TooLarge])]) where [m.Cbor.Readable(errs)]

items.name: put
items.docs: `put(key, value)`: a value of 25 MiB or less (KV throws for more: `KvErr`).

items.name: put_with
items.signature: Kv(a), Str, a, { ttl_ms ?: U64, expires_ms ?: U64, metadata ?: Kv.Metadata } -> Io({}, [Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str)])])
items.docs:
`ttl_ms`: a value under 60 s is raised to 60 s (KV throws for less). `expires_ms`: a time of the clock. `metadata`: made by
`Kv.Metadata.of(m)` (MC5), 1,024 bytes or less as JSON. It is not a type variable of the options: a call with no
`metadata` would leave the type of `m` open, and that does not compile ("type not determined", MODULES.md 5.2).

items.name: put_with!
items.signature: Kv(a), Str, a, { ttl_ms ?: U64, expires_ms ?: U64, metadata ?: Kv.Metadata } => Try({}, [Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str)])])

items.name: list
items.signature: Kv(a), { prefix ?: Str, cursor ?: Str, limit ?: U32 } -> Io({ keys : List(Kv.Key), next : [More(Str), Done] }, [Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown)])])
items.docs: `list`: the keys of one page (1,000 at most). The metadata of a key is CBOR, typed at the use (`Kv.Metadata.parse`).

items.name: list!
items.signature: Kv(a), { prefix ?: Str, cursor ?: Str, limit ?: U32 } => Try({ keys : List(Kv.Key), next : [More(Str), Done] }, [Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown)])])

items.name: Key
items.signature: { name : Str, expires_ms : [Never, At(U64)], metadata : Try(Kv.Metadata, [Missing]) }
items.docs: A key of `list!`.
items.head: Key

items.name: Metadata
items.docs:
The metadata of a key as CBOR. `of` writes it for `put_with!`, `parse` reads it typed at the use (MC7):
`(key.metadata ? |_| Missing).parse()`.
items.head: Metadata

items.name: cell
items.docs: One key as a value: `get!`, `set!` and `delete!` with no key argument (MODULES.md 9).

items.name: find
items.docs: `get` that gives a missing key as `Ok(Err(NotFound))`, so the error type of the caller has no `NotFound`.

items.name: declare
items.signature: Kv.Cell(a) -> { name : Str, kind : Str, props : List((Str, Str)) }
items.docs:
The binding of the cell for the manifest, as `Kv.declare` gives it. Name one cell for each binding: the same
binding name twice in `bindings` is an error at load.

items.name: get_or
items.docs: `get`, and `default` for a key that is not there.

items.name: set_with
items.signature: Kv.Cell(a), a, { ttl_ms ?: U64, expires_ms ?: U64 } -> Io({}, [Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str)])])
items.docs: `ttl_ms`: a value under 60 s is raised to 60 s (KV throws for less). `expires_ms`: a time of the clock.

items.name: set_with!
items.signature: Kv.Cell(a), a, { ttl_ms ?: U64, expires_ms ?: U64 } => Try({}, [Infra([KvErr(Io.Thrown), BadData(Str)])])

items.name: Memo
items.signature: { name : Str, max_age_ms : U64, load! : () => Try(a, e), write : a -> List(U8), read : List(U8) -> Try(a, Str) }
items.head: Memo(a, e)

items.name: new
items.signature: Str, { max_age_ms : U64, load! : () => Try(a, e) } -> Memo(a, e) where [a.Cbor.Writable, a.Cbor.Readable(errs)]
items.docs: A constant (WR1): it does nothing until `get!`. `load!` needs a type annotation (MODULES.md 15).

items.name: get!
items.docs:
The pinned value, else `load!` and a pin of its value. A pinned value that does not parse (an older type of the
same name) loads again. A pin that fails (a full pin table) does not fail `get!`: the value is a cache.

items.name: clear!
items.docs: Drop the pinned value, so the next `get!` loads again.

items.name: zstd_decode!
items.signature: List(U8), U64 => Try(List(U8), [OutputLimit, WindowTooLarge, BadFrame, Truncated, Unsupported])
items.docs:
Decode zstd frames. The output is at most `max_bytes` (MC11): more is `OutputLimit` and no bytes.
A window of any size is fine, because the output is the buffer. Use a `ZstdStream` for a big archive.

items.name: ZstdStream
items.docs: A zstd decoder that takes the archive in chunks. The window limit is 8 MiB (the hard limit too).
items.head: ZstdStream

items.name: open!
items.docs: A stream with the default window limit (8 MiB) and the default limit of one push (16 MiB).

items.name: open_with!
items.signature: { window_limit_bytes ?: U64, push_limit_bytes ?: U64 } => Try(Native.ZstdStream, [BadArgument, TooManyHandles, NoTask])
items.docs: The same with limits. A limit over 8 MiB for the window is `BadArgument`. Zero is the default.

items.name: push!
items.signature: Native.ZstdStream, List(U8) => Try(List(U8), [OutputLimit, WindowTooLarge, BadFrame, Truncated, Unsupported, BadHandle, WrongTask])
items.docs:
The output of the whole blocks in the chunk (it can be empty). After an error the stream stays
dead: each push gives the same error, and `close!` frees it.

items.name: close!
items.signature: Native.ZstdStream => Try({}, [OutputLimit, WindowTooLarge, BadFrame, Truncated, Unsupported, BadHandle, WrongTask])
items.docs: End the input and free the stream, with an error or not. `Truncated`: the input stopped inside a frame.

items.name: Blake3
items.docs: BLAKE3 with state. `final!` frees the state, so a second `final!` or `update!` is `BadHandle`.
items.head: Blake3

items.name: final!
items.docs: The 32 bytes of the digest.

items.name: Sha256
items.docs: SHA-256 with state. The same rules as `Blake3`.
items.head: Sha256

items.name: final!
items.docs: The 32 bytes of the digest.

items.name: Object
items.signature: { namespace : Str, jurisdiction : Str, target : [Named(Str), Id(Str)], location_hint : Str }
items.head: Object(iface)

items.name: namespace
items.signature: Str, { class : Object.Class(iface), script ?: Str } -> Object.Namespace(iface)
items.docs:
A namespace: the binding name and the class of its objects (`class_name` in the Wrangler config). The class is the
value of `Object.class`, so its name is written once, and its interface (`Object.Class(iface)`) is the interface of the
namespace: `call!` takes the `Rpc` constants of that interface only. `script`: the Worker that has the class
(`script_name`), when it is not this Worker. For a class that this app does not have as a value, use
`namespace_named` (this Worker) or `namespace_remote` (another Worker): they take the interface as `Rpc.Iface`.

items.name: namespace_named
items.docs:
A namespace of a class of this Worker, by name: for a class whose `Object.Class` value cannot be imported (a module
cycle). The manifest is the same as `namespace` with that class and no `script`. The shim checks at load that the
class is in `objects`.

items.name: namespace_remote
items.signature: Str, { class : Str, script : Str }, Rpc.Iface(iface) -> Object.Namespace(iface)
items.docs: A namespace of a class that another Worker has (`script_name`): the app has the class name only, as text.

items.name: Namespace
items.signature: { binding : Str, jurisdiction : Str, class : Str, script : Str, iface_name : Str }
items.docs:
A namespace: the binding name, its jurisdiction ("" for none), its class and the Worker of the class ("" for
this Worker), and the name of its interface ("" for a class with no Rpc method). Data.
items.head: Namespace(iface)

items.name: declare
items.signature: Object.Namespace(iface) -> { name : Str, kind : Str, props : List((Str, Str)) }
items.docs:
The binding for the manifest (`Worker.new({ bindings: [...] })`, MODULES.md 3): the kind `object`, with
`class`, `iface` (the interface name, when there is one), and `script` when the class is in another Worker. With
no `script`, the shim checks at load that the class is in `objects`.

items.name: named
items.docs: A stub of the object with this name: `getByName(name)` runs in the program of each call.

items.name: from_id
items.docs: A stub of the object with this id (the text of `id.toString()`): `get(idFromString(id))`.

items.name: unique!
items.docs: `newUniqueId()`, sync (one `call!`). A throw is a crash: the type has no error.

items.name: unique_with!
items.signature: Object.Namespace(iface), { jurisdiction ?: Object.Jurisdiction, location_hint ?: Object.Location } => Try(Object(iface), [Infra([ObjectErr(Io.Thrown)])])
items.docs: `newUniqueId({ jurisdiction })`, sync. The Cloudflare docs recommend `jurisdiction` on the namespace.

items.name: jurisdiction

items.name: to_response
items.docs:
The HTTP response of an object: status 200, the body (a stream, no copy into wasm), the HTTP metadata of the object
(`content-type`, `content-language`, `content-disposition`, `content-encoding`, `cache-control`, `expires`) and
`etag` (`http_etag`). The same headers as `writeHttpMetadata` and `httpEtag` of Workers.

items.name: respond
items.docs:
A GET request answered from the bucket. The key is the argument, the request gives the conditions and the range.
`If-None-Match` and `If-Modified-Since` that fail: 304 with `etag`. `If-Match` and `If-Unmodified-Since` that
fail: 412. A key that is not there: 404. A `Range` of one range (`bytes=a-b`, `bytes=a-`, `bytes=-n`): 206 with
`content-range`, 416 with `content-range: bytes */size` when it starts after the end (R2 error 10039; `respond!` makes the header with one `head!`, the `Io` twin `respond` gives a 416 without it). A request with `If-Range` gets the whole object (R2 has no
`If-Range`). A `Range` that has more than one range, or has a wrong form, is not used. The method is not read:
the app routes GET and HEAD to it. The bytes of a HEAD response are dropped by Workers.

items.name: head
items.docs: The metadata only (`head`).

items.name: put
items.docs:
A body of any kind. A stream with no known length (`Body.writer!`, `compress!`) goes through `pf.r2put`: up to
5 MiB it is one put of the bytes, past it a multipart upload of 5 MiB parts (MODULES.md 5.3).

items.name: put_with
items.signature: R2, Str, Body, { only_if ?: R2.Cond, http ?: R2.Http, custom ?: List((Str, Str)), checksum ?: R2.Checksum, length_bytes ?: U64 } -> Io(R2.Meta, [PreconditionFailed, Infra([R2Err(Io.Thrown)])])
items.docs:
`only_if` makes it a compare and swap: a failed condition is `PreconditionFailed` (R2 gives `null`).
A stream with no known length: as in `put`. Past 5 MiB it is a multipart upload, which takes no `only_if` and no
`checksum` (`R2Err`). `length_bytes`: the stream goes through a `FixedLengthStream` of this length, so it is one
put with each option. A stream of another length is `R2Err`.

reply as one `Packed` value of at most `max` bytes (`pf.pack`). The reply is `{"Ok": value}` or `{"Err": tag}`: its `Err` is

socket is closed) is `Closed`.

items.docs:
The infrastructure errors of the platform, one closed union (MODULES.md 1, MC9). Each platform function gives
its own tags in `Infra(...)`. The `err` of a method closes them: `[NotOpen, Infra(Rpc.Infra)]`. A SQL constraint
failure is not here: it is the flat domain tag `Constraint(Sql.Constraint)`, which a method lists in its `err` when it
passes it on (`[NotOpen, Constraint(Sql.Constraint), Infra(Rpc.Infra)]`).
items.head: Infra

items.docs:
A nested call in a handler, for `?`: `call!(...) ? Rpc.forward(f)`. The errors of this call stay in `Infra`,
`f` maps the `err` of the callee (`Rpc.forward(|e| e)` when the two methods have one error type).

items.name: Iface
items.docs:
An interface (MODULES.md 8): a type of the app with no values (`Ledger := []`) and its name as text. The shared module
of the Workers makes one value for each interface (`ledger : Rpc.Iface(Ledger)`, `ledger = Rpc.iface("Ledger")`).
The type connects the two sides of a call in the compiler. The name goes to the manifest: the type cannot cross a
Worker (the link of a service binding or of a `namespace_remote` is in the Wrangler config), so `roc-cloudflare-workers
sync` compares the names of the Workers of one repo. A call with no `Iface`, or with the `Iface` of another interface,
does not compile.
items.head: Iface(iface)

items.name: method
items.signature: Rpc.Iface(iface), Str -> Rpc(iface, arg, ret, err)
items.docs:
A method of the interface (WR1): the method name and, by the annotation of the constant, the types of both sides.
`err` is the tag union that the callee can give (`Rpc.NoErr` for none): the caller gets it as `Remote(err)`.
A method that two interfaces serve is a function of the interface: `ping : Rpc.Iface(iface) -> Rpc(iface, {}, Str, Rpc.NoErr)`,
`ping = |i| i.method("ping")`.

items.name: name
items.docs: The name that `Rpc.iface` got.

items.name: iface
items.docs:
The value of an interface: `ledger = Rpc.iface("Ledger")`. The name is the name of the type, as text. Two values with
the same name and different types are two interfaces for the compiler and one for `sync`.

items.docs:
The distinct interface names of some handlers, in order: none for no handler. A class, a Worker and an entry point
have one name at most: two names are an error at load (`checkManifest` in `js/manifest.js`).

A named entry point (a `WorkerEntrypoint` class): `export const Admin = entrypointClass("Admin")` in the JS entry
file. A service binding with `entrypoint = "Admin"` reaches it. Its `fetch!` gets the requests of `Service.fetch!`
on that binding (the event `EntrypointFetch`). With no `fetch!`, the class has no `fetch` method in JS.

the same shape. `Try` has no codec, so the wire form is its own type. `reply_of` parses it, `on` writes its bytes.

A secret (MODULES.md 10). `Str.inspect` shows `Secret(...)`, and only `reveal` gives the text. It has no codec, so a
`Log` line or typed data (CBOR) with a secret in it does not compile (`conformance/must-not-compile/`).
The backing is a record: an opaque type over a bare `Str` gets the codecs of `Str` (roc-lang/roc#12309, MODULES.md 15).

MODULES.md 5.1, "Constraint kinds": the message ends in `: SQLITE_CONSTRAINT`, or in
`: SQLITE_CONSTRAINT (extended: <code>)`. The kind comes from the code, not from the text: a `RAISE` text can look like
another failure. `message` is the SQLite text with no `D1_ERROR: ` (or `D1_EXEC_ERROR: `) and no code.

items.name: connect
items.docs: `connect({ hostname, port })`, then a wait for `opened`: one wait. A host that does not answer is `SocketErr`.

items.name: read
items.docs:
The next bytes that the peer sent, at most `Body.default_max` (MC11: the rest comes next). One wait, with no
deadline (API.md 10.2). `Closed` at the end of the stream. In `Io.race!`, a branch that lost takes no bytes (OP8).

items.name: write
items.docs: `writer.write(bytes)`: one wait. A socket that is closed is `Closed`.

items.name: start_tls
items.docs:

is not usable after it.

items.name: close!
items.docs: `socket.close()`, one `call!` with no wait. A throw is dropped.

items.name: now_ms!
items.docs: `Date.now()`: one `call!`, no wait. On the edge it is coarse: it moves only at I/O.

items.name: sleep
items.docs:
`scheduler.wait(ms)`: one wait. The timer stops when the signal of the task aborts (the end of the task, or a
lost branch of `Io.race!`, OP8). The error type is open, so the twin joins the errors of the other branches.

(`One(Raw)` for an AES or HMAC key, `Pair({ private: Pkcs8, public: Spki })` for the others).

items.signature: WebCrypto.KeyAlg, { modulus_bits ?: U32, length_bits ?: U32 } -> Io(WebCrypto.Generated, [Infra([CryptoErr(Io.Thrown)])])
items.docs:
`modulus_bits`: RSA (default 2048, the public exponent is 65537). `length_bits`: AES (default 256) and HMAC (default:
the block size of the hash). PBKDF2 and HKDF have no `generateKey`: `CryptoErr`.

items.name: generate_key_with!
items.signature: WebCrypto.KeyAlg, { modulus_bits ?: U32, length_bits ?: U32 } => Try(WebCrypto.Generated, [Infra([CryptoErr(Io.Thrown)])])

items.name: hmac_sha256
items.docs: HMAC-SHA256 in Roc over the builtin SHA-256 (RFC 2104): no crossing, no wait (RN9: the webhook signature).

items.name: sha256!
items.docs:
SHA-256 of bytes in wasm memory: the builtin `Crypto.SHA256` below `sha256_crossover_bytes` (no crossing), else
`crypto.subtle.digest` (one crossing, one wait, the isolate runs other tasks meanwhile). The result is the 32 bytes of
the digest. For a body that is not in wasm memory yet, use `Body.sha256!`.

items.name: sha256
items.docs:
The twin of `sha256!` (MC3). Below the crossover its program has no op: a `Io.run!` of it is one `call!` of an
empty program, and inside `Io.both!` it is a branch with no op.

items.name: timing_safe_equal!
items.docs: `crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual`: one `call!`, no wait. Texts of different lengths are not equal (no crossing).

items.name: random!
items.docs: `crypto.getRandomValues`: `n` new random bytes, one `call!` for each 65,536 bytes (the limit of Workers).

items.name: random_uuid!
items.docs: `crypto.randomUUID`: one `call!`, no wait.

items.name: Key
items.docs: The material of a key, or a ref of the task (`import_key!`, MC13).
items.head: Key

items.signature: [Hmac(WebCrypto.Hash), RsaPkcs1(WebCrypto.Hash), RsaPss({ hash : WebCrypto.Hash, salt_length_bytes : U32 }), Ecdsa(WebCrypto.Curve, WebCrypto.Hash), Ed25519]
items.head: Alg

items.name: Cipher
items.signature: [AesGcm({ iv : List(U8) }), AesCbc({ iv : List(U8) }), AesCtr({ counter : List(U8), length_bits : U32 }), RsaOaep({ label : List(U8), hash : WebCrypto.Hash })]
items.docs: `RsaOaep` has a `hash`: `importKey` of an RSA-OAEP key needs one, and a key as data has none (MODULES.md 10).
items.head: Cipher

items.signature: [Pbkdf2({ salt : List(U8), iterations : U32, hash : WebCrypto.Hash }), Hkdf({ salt : List(U8), info : List(U8), hash : WebCrypto.Hash }), Ecdh({ curve : WebCrypto.Curve, public : WebCrypto.Key }), X25519({ public : WebCrypto.Key })]

items.name: is_eq
items.docs: Two values are the same socket when they hold the same ref (API.md RS1).

items.name: Message
items.docs: One frame. `json` parses a text frame as JSON, the format of most WebSocket clients.
items.head: Message

items.name: Closed
items.signature: { code : U16, reason : Str, clean : Bool }
items.docs: The close of a socket: the code and the reason of the close frame, and `clean` (`wasClean`).
items.head: Closed

items.name: is_upgrade
items.docs: The request asks for a WebSocket: its `Upgrade` header is `websocket` (the case does not matter).

items.name: accept!
items.signature: Request => Try({ socket : WebSocket, response : Response }, [NotUpgrade])
items.docs:
`new WebSocketPair()`, `accept()` of the server end, and a 101 response with the client end, in one `call!`.
Give `response.after(work!)` with a `receive!` loop in the work: a 101 response keeps the task until the socket
closes (API.md 10.2). `NotUpgrade` when the request has no `Upgrade: websocket`.

items.name: connect
items.docs:
A client: `fetch(url)` with `Upgrade: websocket`, then `accept()` of the `webSocket` of the response, in one
program with one wait. A `ws://` or `wss://` URL is sent as `http://` or `https://` (the `fetch` of Workers takes
only these). `NotUpgrade` when the server does not answer 101. A throw of `fetch` is `SocketErr`.

items.name: connect_with
items.signature: Str, { headers ?: List(Header), protocols ?: List(Str) } -> Io(WebSocket, [NotUpgrade, Infra([SocketErr(Io.Thrown)])])
items.docs: `headers`: more request headers. `protocols`: the header `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`.

items.name: connect_with!
items.signature: Str, { headers ?: List(Header), protocols ?: List(Str) } => Try(WebSocket, [NotUpgrade, Infra([SocketErr(Io.Thrown)])])

items.name: send!
items.docs: `ws.send(data)`, one `call!`. A throw (the socket is closed) is `Closed`.

items.name: send_json!
items.docs:
The value as JSON text, in a text frame. A value that JSON cannot show (a `NaN` in an `F64`) is `BadData`, and
nothing is sent.

items.name: receive
items.docs:
The next message: one wait (`pf.wsReceive`), with no deadline (API.md 10.2). After the close, each call gives
`Closed`. In `Io.race!`, a branch that lost takes no message: it stays for the next call (OP8).

items.name: close!
items.docs: `ws.close(code, reason)`, one `call!`. A throw (a code that the app cannot send, a closed socket) is dropped.

items.name: Worker
items.signature:
{
	handlers : List(Str),
	own! : Worker.Event => Worker.Outcome,
	rpc : List(Rpc.Handler({})),
	entrypoints : List(Rpc.Entrypoint),
	objects : List(Object.AnyClass),
	bindings : List(Worker.Binding),
	crons : List(Str),
}
items.docs:
`handlers`: the handlers of the default export that the app gives (the manifest). `own!`: runs the events of those
handlers (`Fetch`, `Scheduled`, `Queue`, `Email`, `Tail`, `Other`). `bindings` and `crons`: for the manifest only.
items.head: Worker

items.name: new
items.signature:
{
		fetch! ?: Request => Try(Response, e1),
		scheduled! ?: Worker.Scheduled => Try({}, e2),
		queue! ?: Queue.Batch => Try({}, e3),
		email! ?: Email.Mail => Try({}, e4),
		tail! ?: List(Worker.TraceItem) => Try({}, e5),
		other! ?: Str, Js => Try(Js, e6),
		rpc ?: List(Rpc.Serves(iface, {})),
		entrypoints ?: List(Rpc.Entrypoint),
		objects ?: List(Object.AnyClass),
		bindings ?: List(Worker.Binding),
		crons ?: List(Worker.Cron),
	} -> Worker
items.docs: The handlers of the app. A function, not a record literal: each handler keeps its own error type until here.

items.name: cron
items.docs:
A handler for one cron expression (`triggers.crons` of the Wrangler config). A run of another cron goes to
`scheduled!`. The expression is in the manifest, so `roc-cloudflare-workers sync` checks the config.

items.name: Cron
items.docs: A cron handler with its error type erased.
items.head: Cron

items.name: Binding
items.signature: { name : Str, kind : Str, props : List((Str, Str)) }
items.docs:
A binding that the app uses (`db.declare()`, `rooms.declare()`, ...), for the manifest: the name in `env`, the
kind, and the settings of the kind (`class` and `script` of an object namespace, `service` and `entrypoint` of a
service). The shim checks at load that `env` has each one with its kind.
items.head: Binding

items.name: Event
items.signature:
[
		Fetch(Request),
		Scheduled(Worker.Scheduled),
		Queue(Queue.Batch),
		Email(Email.Mail),
		Rpc({ entrypoint : Str, method : Str, arg : List(U8) }),
		EntrypointFetch({ entrypoint : Str, request : Request }),
		Object({ class : Str, id : Str, event : Object.Event }),
		Tail(List(Worker.TraceItem)),
		Other({ kind : Str, payload : Js }),
		Manifest,
	]
items.docs:
One event of Workers (API.md 10.1). Phase A has all tags. The shim sends `Fetch`, `Scheduled`, `Other`, and since
PLAN.md 8f `Rpc`, `EntrypointFetch`, `Object` and `Manifest`.
items.head: Event

items.name: Outcome
items.docs: What the app gives back for an event (API.md 10.1).
items.head: Outcome

items.name: Scheduled
items.docs: The payload of a cron run (MODULES.md 3). `time_ms` is `controller.scheduledTime`, the planned time.
items.head: Scheduled

items.name: new
items.docs: Plain data (MC13): a test can make one.

items.name: no_retry!
items.docs:
`controller.noRetry()`, one `call!` with no wait. The shim never calls it by itself (MODULES.md 3).
A throw is dropped: only a `Worker.Scheduled` of a `Scheduled` event has a controller.

items.name: TraceItem
items.signature:
{
		script_name : Try(Str, [Missing]),
		outcome : Str,
		event_timestamp_ms : Try(U64, [Missing]),
		event : Try({ request : { method : Str, url : Str, headers : List({ name : Str, value : Str }), cf : Try(Request.Cf, [Missing]) }, response : Try({ status : U16 }, [Missing]) }, [Missing]),
		logs : List({ timestamp_ms : U64, level : Str, message : Str }),
		exceptions : List({ timestamp_ms : U64, name : Str, message : Str }),
	}
items.docs:
One item of the batch of a Tail Worker (MODULES.md 3): plain data, read as CBOR (MC5, PLAN.md 8f).
`parser_for : _`: a nominal type opts in to the derived parser (MODULES.md 15). The request headers are records of
`name` and `value`, not `Header` of `roc-lang/http`: that type has no `parser_for` (PLAN.md 8b O1).
items.head: TraceItem

items.name: event
items.signature: Worker.TraceItem -> Try({ request : { method : Str, url : Str, headers : List({ name : Str, value : Str }), cf : Try(Request.Cf, [Missing]) }, response : Try({ status : U16 }, [Missing]) }, [Missing])

items.signature: Worker.TraceItem -> List({ timestamp_ms : U64, name : Str, message : Str })

items.name: event!
items.docs:
The one entry, made from the handlers that the app gives (`event! = |e| worker.event!(e)`).
A missing handler gives `Unhandled`. An `Err(e)` gives `Failed` with `Str.inspect(e)`.
